subject.title: Feishu: bot does not respond when @-mentioned in a reply message

question: Should maintainers adopt or replace the conflicting fork PR for this issue, or ask the fork author to rebase and prove it before any new repair is queued?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but an open fork PR already claims it with closing syntax and the same-repository version of that branch was closed unmerged with prior routing and gating concerns; automation should not create a duplicate fix until maintainers choose the path.

options.title: Adopt or replace with a narrow current-main fix
options.body: Use the existing branch only as context, then land a current-main Feishu plugin fix with bot-specific mention evidence and scope-aware routing tests.

options.title: Wait for the fork author
options.body: Keep this issue open while asking the fork author to rebase the conflicting branch and add inspectable Feishu proof plus routing-safety changes.

options.title: Defer to Feishu plugin ownership
options.body: Leave this as an open Feishu channel bug until the declared plugin contact or another owner can handle the fix manually.

recommendation.title: Adopt or replace with a narrow current-main fix
recommendation.body: Use the existing branch only as context, then land a current-main Feishu plugin fix with bot-specific mention evidence and scope-aware routing tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is confined to the declared Feishu/Lark plugin boundary and affects Feishu channel mention/routing behavior.
